reader_questions: Who must apply for a Korea Residence Card and what is the 90-day deadline?
Is ARC still the correct name for the physical foreign resident ID?
Which immigration office should I reserve and does the reservation satisfy the deadline?
What documents and photo specifications are required for a first application?

Can I open a bank account or leave Korea before the physical card arrives?

sources.name: Ministry of Justice Foreigner Registration Card Basics
factual_notes: A foreign national intending to stay more than 90 days must register within 90 days of entry.
Applicants reserve on HiKorea and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over the place of residence.
The general document set includes passport, proof of residence, one 3.5 by 4.5 centimeter photo, and status-specific documents.
The photo must be recent within six months, front-facing, and use a plain or white borderless background.

sources.name: HiKorea e-Government for Foreigners
factual_notes: HiKorea is the official portal used for immigration visit reservations, e-Applications, forms, and current service notices.
A reservation selects an office and time but is not itself completion of foreigner registration.

sources.name: Korea Immigration Service Residence Card Fee Increase
factual_notes: The new issuance fee is KRW 35,000 from January 1, 2025.
New cards include an IC chip used for Mobile Residence Card setup.
Existing valid cards did not require replacement solely because of the new design; voluntary reissue uses the new fee.

sources.name: Korea Immigration Service 1345 Contact Center
factual_notes: 1345 provides multilingual immigration and Korea-living counseling on weekdays from 09:00 to 22:00.
After 18:00, Korean, English, and Chinese are available.
The service can provide immigration-office jurisdiction and service-hour information.

sources.name: Ministry of Justice Visa Navigator and Reporting Obligations
factual_notes: Registered foreigners must report a change of residence within 15 days to the relevant immigration office or community service center.
Registration-detail changes are generally reported within 15 days, while passport changes are reported within 45 days under the guide.
International students need advance permission for covered part-time work, and workplace changes can require permission or reporting.

sources.name: Ministry of Justice 2026 Employment Information Reporting Guide
factual_notes: From January 2, 2026, foreign nationals engaged in for-profit activity under listed statuses must report occupation, industry, and annual income bracket.
The listed statuses include D-7 to D-9, E-1 to E-10, F-2, F-4, F-6, and H-2, excluding F-5 from this reporting program.
Initial and changed employment information can be submitted through HiKorea, and changes must generally be reported within 15 days.

sources.name: Ministry of Justice Mobile Residence Card Press Release
factual_notes: Registered foreign nationals age 14 and older with a smartphone registered in their name can use the Mobile Residence Card.
New IC-card holders can set it up by tapping the card, entering the PIN, and completing face authentication.
Older physical-card holders must visit an immigration office or branch for QR-based setup.
Only one smartphone can hold the Mobile Residence Card.

sources.name: National Health Insurance Service Guidance for Foreigners
factual_notes: Foreign residents working at covered workplaces can be compulsorily enrolled through employment.
Many eligible self-employed foreign residents are subject to mandatory health insurance after staying more than six months, depending on status and exceptions.
National health insurance coverage for enrolled foreign residents is described as the same coverage provided to Korean citizens.
